extraction.name: Video-MME
extraction.description: Video-MME is the first comprehensive Multi-Modal Evaluation benchmark for assessing Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in video analysis. It consists of 900 manually curated videos spanning 6 primary visual domains and 30 subfields, annotated with 2,700 high-quality multiple-choice question-answer pairs covering short, medium, and long videos ranging from 11 seconds to 1 hour. The benchmark incorporates multi-modal inputs including video frames, subtitles, and audio tracks to enable all-round evaluation of MLLMs.
extraction.creator: Chaoyou Fu; Yuhan Dai; Yongdong Luo; Lei Li; Shuhuai Ren; Renrui Zhang; Zihan Wang; Chenyu Zhou; Yunhang Shen; Mengdan Zhang; Peixian Chen; Yanwei Li; Shaohui Lin; Sirui Zhao; Ke Li; Tong Xu; Xiawu Zheng; Enhong Chen; Caifeng Shan; Ran He; Xing Sun
extraction.citeAs: Chaoyou Fu, Yuhan Dai, Yongdong Luo, Lei Li, Shuhuai Ren, Renrui Zhang, Zihan Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Yunhang Shen, Mengdan Zhang, Peixian Chen, Yanwei Li, Shaohui Lin, Sirui Zhao, Ke Li, Tong Xu, Xiawu Zheng, Enhong Chen, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Xing Sun. Video-MME: The First-Ever Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark of Multi-modal LLMs in Video Analysis. arXiv:2405.21075, 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Videos were manually collected from YouTube across 6 key domains and 30 fine-grained categories. For each category, videos of varying durations (short: <2 minutes, medium: 4-15 minutes, long: 30-60 minutes) were collected along with corresponding meta-information including subtitles (if provided) and audio tracks.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Not all videos had subtitles available; the dataset contains 744 videos with subtitles out of 900 total videos, meaning 156 videos lacked subtitle information.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: YouTube videos spanning 6 primary visual domains (Knowledge, Film & Television, Sports Competition, Artistic Performance, Life Record, and Multilingual) with 30 fine-grained subcategories, along with associated subtitle files and audio tracks.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning were recruited. Each annotator thoroughly viewed the entire video, then created three multiple-choice questions, each with four candidate options, for a total of 2,700 QA pairs. A quality review was conducted where each QA pair was examined by a different annotator to verify clarity of language, answerability, logical consistency of options, and appropriateness of the correct answer. QA pairs that could be answered without video content were filtered out using Gemini 1.5 Pro in a text-only setup and returned to the original annotator for revision.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Each QA pair was reviewed by a different annotator to verify quality. Additionally, Gemini 1.5 Pro was used to filter out QA pairs answerable from text alone (achieving less than 15% accuracy in text-only setup), ensuring video content was required to answer questions.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Strong English proficiency; extensive research experience in vision-language learning
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini 1.5 Pro (used to filter QA pairs answerable without video content)
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Existing open-source models fix the number of input frames (e.g., 8 frames), resulting in excessively sparse information density as video length increases; a general decline in MLLM performance is observed as video duration increases for all models; limitations in processing longer video sequences could be a critical bottleneck in the performance of MLLMs
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Comprehensive evaluation of MLLMs on video understanding tasks; benchmarking multi-modal large language models across diverse video types, temporal durations, and data modalities; evaluating both image and video MLLMs on sequential visual data understanding
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: QA pairs that could be answered solely based on textual questions (without video content) were filtered out using Gemini 1.5 Pro in a text-only setup; questions not meeting the video-content requirement were returned to annotators for revision. Each QA pair also underwent examination by a different annotator to verify clarity of language expression, logical consistency of candidate options, and appropriateness of the correct answer.
